author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: The veterinarian directory can be narrowed to a single specialty on both surfaces: the page staff read, and the machine-readable form, which becomes a supported surface. Matching is on the whole specialty name, disregarding letter case. A narrowed page stays paged. Naming no specialty, or spaces alone, publishes every veterinarian.
acceptance_criteria: Given no specialty named, when either surface is requested, then it publishes every veterinarian as it does today.
Given a specialty veterinarians hold, when the page is requested for it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time.
Given a narrowed page, when a later page of it is requested, then that page lists further veterinarians holding the same specialty.
Given a specialty veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable form is requested for it, then it carries only those veterinarians.
Given a specialty named in different letter case, when either surface is requested, then it matches the specialty as held.
Given a specialty named as a prefix of a held specialty, when either surface is requested, then it does not match.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested, then the request succeeds and no veterinarian is listed.
Given a specialty named as empty or as spaces alone, when either surface is requested, then every veterinarian is published.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed when any one of them is named.
Edge case 3: a specialty named with surrounding spaces matches nothing, because the whole name must match.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search, which NG-9 still declines.
A form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface.
Paging the machine-readable directory; it carries every matching veterinarian in one document.
Narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty.
notes: NG-9 narrowed and REQ-VET-003 minted; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. Rationale lives in docs/adr/2026-08-12-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than consulted: a visible control, whether spaces around a named specialty should be disregarded, and whether the machine-readable form should be paged. Each took the narrowest reading of the request. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope and still needs adding.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Narrow non-goal NG-9: free-text veterinarian search remains out of scope; filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows (specialty) is in scope. Record the narrowing the way this project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A small extension of the existing vet directory, not new ground. Both handlers in VetController gain an optional specialty request parameter and choose between today's unfiltered repository call and one new specialty-narrowed derived query. No new package, type, layer, or pattern: this is the shape OwnerController already uses for last-name search, recorded in docs/system-design.md under Contracts and Package Structure. Whole-name, case-insensitive matching belongs in the Spring Data query method name (IgnoreCase), never in the controller; the controller's only decision is which repository method to call, which the architecture-principles Web controller row admits as request binding rather than a business rule. The absent-parameter path must stay exactly as today, so the @Cacheable findAll reads, their keys, and their paging are untouched. Rejected alternative: a single conditional JPQL query with ':specialty is null or ...', because it would need a left join plus distinct, would change the unfiltered path's SQL and paging, and would bypass the vets cache. Resolution basis: read of the vet package and grep of the owner precedent; no IDE oracle is connected in this run, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetController to VetRepository: two new derived query methods — a paged one for /vets.html and a Collection one for /vets. Suggested names findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String), both @Transactional(readOnly = true) like their neighbours. Existing findAll calls stay on the absent-parameter path.
VetController to vets/vetList.html: a new model attribute named specialty, consumed by every pagination link so a later page stays narrowed.
vet package to system CacheConfiguration: the new query methods stay outside the vets cache; the two findAll methods keep their @Cacheable annotations unchanged.
No new cross-package dependency. The vet package still depends only on model, so the acyclic graph in docs/system-design.md holds.

patterns.description: Derived paged query on a declarative Spring Data Repository interface — the shape the specialty query follows. Note the vet property path crosses a ManyToMany collection: Vet.specialties then the inherited NamedEntity.name, so spell it with the underscore separator.
Optional filter parameter normalized, then delegated to the repository. Follow the delegation shape, not the strip() on line 103 — see the risk on padded values.
findPaginated helper to extend with the specialty argument; addPaginationModel is where the specialty model attribute belongs.
@DataJpaTest with an autowired VetRepository against seeded H2 — the home for the matching-semantics tests. The seed gives radiology, surgery and dentistry, and vet 3 holds two specialties.
The pagination block: five link forms, each needing the specialty carried through.

risks.risk: Thymeleaf expression injection: extending the template's existing '__${...}__' preprocessing to the request-supplied specialty would evaluate that value as an OGNL/SpEL expression and skip URL encoding.
risks.mitigation: Build the links with link-expression parameters — @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} — so Thymeleaf encodes the value. Keep '__...__' preprocessing off any request-supplied value. A specialty containing a space or an ampersand is the functional test of this.

risks.risk: Unbounded cache growth: annotating a specialty-keyed method @Cacheable("vets") gives that cache a caller-controlled key space, and CacheConfiguration sets no size limit (its own javadoc says the limit must come from the JCache provider, and none is configured). Arbitrary query values would grow the heap.
risks.mitigation: Leave both new query methods uncached. @Cacheable stays on the two findAll methods only. This also keeps the slice clear of Open Question 5 (vet cache invalidation) in docs/system-design.md.

risks.risk: Duplicate rows under paging: specialties.name carries a plain index, not a unique constraint, so a vet holding two same-named specialties would appear twice in the joined page and distort the page count.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived query name so the select and its count query are per-vet.

risks.risk: Vendor-dependent case handling: the PostgreSQL owner-search defect in docs/system-design.md Known Defects comes from leaning on column collation for case-insensitivity.
risks.mitigation: Get case-insensitivity from the derived IgnoreCase keyword, which renders upper(...) = upper(?) in JPQL and holds identically on H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL. Change no schema and no collation.

risks.risk: Vacuous acceptance tests: VetControllerTests mocks VetRepository, so case-insensitivity, prefix non-match, the padded-space case and the multi-specialty case would assert only the stub's behaviour.
risks.mitigation: Assert those four in ClinicServiceTests against the real H2 seed. Keep VetControllerTests for parameter binding, the blank-is-absent rule, the paging model, the pagination links, and the JSON body.

risks.risk: Wrong-way convergence on trimming: the owner precedent strips its filter value, but this slice requires a padded specialty to match nothing.
risks.mitigation: Pass the parameter through unchanged. Use only a hasText check to choose filtered versus unfiltered, and pin the divergence with theVetDirectoryPageShouldNotMatchASpecialtyNamePaddedWithSpaces so no later reader 'fixes' it.

risks.risk: Filter lost on page two: the owner list template drops its filter from page links, and copying that block verbatim would break the later-page criterion.
risks.mitigation: Carry specialty through all five link forms in vetList.html, including first, previous, next and last.

notes:
Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix and no prd-autofix records exist since the prd-entry, so nothing to judge.

Durable-memory writes made with this triage. docs/adr/README.md gained the missing index row for 2026-08-12-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md (the gap the PRD author flagged as outside their write scope). docs/system-design.md: the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement is removed, because REQ-VET-003 makes that surface supported; the Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository and VetController now cite REQ-VET-003. Purpose text for those rows describes the pre-filter state and is left to doc-sync after the slice lands.

No ADR this slice. The product decision already has one (the non-goal ADR), and the remaining choices are all cheaply reversible, so none clears the hard-to-reverse bar. The uncached-filtered-reads fact is a state statement doc-sync can add to docs/system-design.md without an ADR back-link.

Open questions, narrowest reading, as instructed. No visible control on either surface, so no new user-facing text and no new message keys — REQ-LANG-002's bundle-versus-template test stays green only if the template gains no literal text. No trimming of a non-empty value. The JSON surface stays unpaged and carries every match in one document.

Blank handling in one place: read the parameter as @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty and let a single private helper decide, so the rule is not duplicated across the two handlers. Duplicating it would start to look like a business rule living in the controller, which the architecture-principles checklist forbids for new rules.

One detail to settle with a test rather than by assumption: how the link expression renders a null specialty. Either rendering satisfies the criteria, because an empty value is treated as absent, but assert whichever the template produces.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: the NVD match did not run in this review - build.gradle configures no org.owasp.dependencycheck plugin (the CycloneDX BOM plugin generates an SBOM but matches nothing), and the reviewer has no network. This change adds no dependency, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged; treat the Spring Boot 4.1.0 CVE check as open for CI or a human to close, not as clean.

Pattern consistency: expression preprocessing of the same shape this change retired still lives in owners/ownersList.html (lines 44, 49, 54), owners/ownerDetails.html, and fragments/layout.html. None is exploitable today - those values are ints bound from @RequestParam, entity identifiers, or fixed fragment arguments - so this is not a defect in this change. Converting them to link-expression parameters would leave one way per concern instead of two.

No pagination bound: /vets.html?page= still accepts any int, unchanged by this diff (a negative page reaches PageRequest.of and raises). Pre-existing, noted so it is not mistaken for something this change introduced.
approved_aspects: Thymeleaf expression injection closed: all five pagination links in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html (lines 30, 35, 40, 46, 52) were converted from expression preprocessing to link-expression parameters @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. A grep -F sweep for '__' across src/main/resources/templates/ confirms no preprocessing remains in vetList.html. Link-expression parameters are URL-encoded and the attribute value is HTML-escaped, so the caller-supplied specialty is never evaluated as an expression - VetControllerTests.theVetDirectoryPageShouldNotEvaluateTheNamedSpecialtyAsATemplateExpression pins this with a literal-breaking payload.

Unbounded cache growth closed: CacheConfiguration (system/CacheConfiguration.java) still creates the 'vets' cache with no size limit, and @Cacheable("vets") remains on findAll() and findAll(Pageable) only. Both new methods findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String) and (String, Pageable) are uncached, with the reason recorded in their Javadoc. The caller-supplied specialty therefore never becomes a cache key, so the caller cannot drive the key space.

Query injection closed: matching runs through the Spring Data derived query name findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, which the framework translates to a bound-parameter criteria query. A sweep for @Query and createQuery across src/main/java finds only the pre-existing static PetTypeRepository JPQL - no string-built query text carries a request-derived value. This satisfies security-principles.md 'Injection into data access'.

Reflected XSS: the specialty value reaches the rendered page only as a link-expression query parameter (URL-encoded, then attribute-escaped). It is not rendered as text, and a sweep finds no th:utext anywhere under src/main/resources/templates/. Thymeleaf default escaping stays on, matching the system-design.md threat-model row for XSS.

DoS shape assessed as no worse than baseline: the specialty value is a bound parameter to an equality comparison (no regex, so no ReDoS) and the query string is capped by the container's header limit. The filtered result set is a subset of the pre-existing unfiltered findAll(), so the unpaged /vets JSON response cannot grow beyond what that route already returns. Skipping the cache costs a database round trip per request, which is the correct trade against a caller-controlled key space in an unbounded cache.

Boundary handling: StringUtils.hasText treats absent, empty, and whitespace-only values as naming no specialty, so a blank parameter degrades to the unfiltered directory rather than an error. No new logging, no new exception message, no request-derived value reaching a filesystem or resource path, and no new dependency.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: One module, no sensitive paths, 79 production lines across three files all inside the vet package plus its template; the only reach beyond the new feature is vetList.html, which every directory reader hits whether or not a specialty is named.

semantic_surprise.note: The five pagination links were rewritten from preprocessed URLs to link-expression parameters, and Thymeleaf's StandardLinkBuilder appends a bare parameter name when the value is null (verified in processAllRemainingParametersAsQueryParams), so the unfiltered directory's links now render /vets.html?page=N&specialty rather than /vets.html?page=N; binding still degrades to the unfiltered list because the empty value fails hasText, but the URL surface of an untouched page changed and no record mentions it.

test_adequacy.note: Repository tests run against real seeded H2 data and pin case-insensitivity, prefix non-match, padded non-match, multi-specialty membership and distinct paged counts, and the controller tests key their stubs to eq() matchers so a trimming regression would fail rather than pass; the one soft spot is theVetDirectoryPageShouldOfferALaterPageWhenNoSpecialtyIsNamed, whose containsString("/vets.html?page=2") prefix match cannot distinguish the changed unfiltered URL.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved in round 2, but the security-reviewer's approval carries recommendations that explicitly do not close: the Spring Boot 4.1.0 CVE check never ran (no dependency-check plugin, no network) and is handed to CI or a human as open rather than clean, alongside carried-forward notes on preprocessing still living in the owners templates and an unbounded page parameter.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the ADR-narrowed NG-9 and the new REQ-VET-003 acceptance criteria with nothing extra; the three product defaults the owner declined to decide (no trim, no visible control, unpaged JSON) are implemented in one direction and each is recorded as an open question, and the row's build_retries of 0 reflects the counter resetting after the superseded design-block rather than a slice that never failed.

rationale: Every pagination link on the unfiltered directory now renders /vets.html?page=N&specialty, because Thymeleaf emits a bare parameter name for a null value, and the one test covering that URL matches only its prefix. Behaviour is unaffected; the URL surface is not. Confirm that, and the unrun CVE check.
